page: Vultr vx1-m-96c-768gb is a memory-optimized instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD x86_64 CPU architecture and provides 768.0 GB of system memory. With an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance provides a 1:8 core-to-memory configuration designed for large-scale memory-bound applications. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated hardware GPU acceleration.

Local disk provisioning is set to 1 GB of NVMe SSD storage. Because this baseline local storage footprint is minimal, workloads requiring persistent data storage or local temporary disk caching require external attached storage volumes. The resource profile provides dedicated compute cores, eliminating multi-tenant thread contention across heavy computational processes while granting full access to its high-capacity memory space.

The vx1-m-96c-768gb configuration is tailored for workloads requiring substantial RAM footprints coupled with dense multithreaded processing capacity. Typical applications include large distributed in-memory databases, enterprise key-value caching layers, large-scale graph databases, and extensive extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines where large datasets must be retained in memory.

With zero dedicated GPUs present, computational execution is sustained entirely by the dedicated AMD processor cores. This dense CPU and memory combination fits memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases, enterprise-grade caching platforms, and data analytics pipelines.
